correctness.rationale: For 0!=j in J(R), 0 and j are false twins, obstructing 2-existential closure. Reduced finite commutative rings split into fields; single-field cliques and binary coordinates obstruct 2-ec. In the remaining t>=2,q_i>=3 case, exact inclusion-exclusion counts for distinct anchor pair a,b are c11=W, c10=c01=U-W-epsilon, c00=N-2U+W-2(1-epsilon), where W=prod_equal(q_i-1)prod_differ(q_i-2), U=prod(q_i-1), N=prod(q_i), epsilon=1 when anchors differ in all coordinates. Positivity establishes 2-ec; classifying which counts can equal 1 gives 2-ec-critical iff t=2 and some q_i=3 or t>=3 all q_i=3. A hybrid of two mutually coordinate-different anchors forces adjacency to any common neighbor, defeating 3-ec. Infinite-duration three-pebble back-and-forth uses exactly two anchored vertices, establishing FO^3 equivalence; a four-variable extension sentence separates FO^4. Independent explicit finite counts for six field products matched, but do not prove the arbitrary-ring assertions.
